In [[mathematics]], especially in the area of [[abstract algebra|algebra]] known as [[ring theory]], an '''Ore extension''', named after [[Øystein Ore]], is a special type of a [[ring extension]] whose properties are relatively well understood. Elements of a Ore extension are called '''Ore polynomials'''. 

Ore extensions appear in several natural contexts, including skew and differential [[polynomial ring]]s, [[group ring|group algebra]]s of [[polycyclic group]]s, [[universal enveloping algebra]]s of [[solvable Lie algebra]]s, and [[coordinate ring]]s of [[quantum group]]s.

== Definition ==

Suppose that ''R'' is a (not necessarily [[commutative ring|commutative]]) [[ring (mathematics)|ring]], <math>\sigma \colon R \to R</math> is a [[ring homomorphism]], and <math>\delta\colon R\to R</math> is a ''' ''σ''-derivation''' of ''R'', which means that <math>\delta</math> is a [[group homomorphism|homomorphism]] of [[abelian group]]s satisfying

: <math>\delta(r_1 r_2) = \sigma(r_1)\delta(r_2)+\delta(r_1)r_2</math>.

Then the '''Ore extension''' <math>R[x;\sigma,\delta]</math>, also called a '''skew polynomial ring''', is the [[noncommutative ring]] obtained by giving the [[polynomial ring|ring of polynomials]] <math>R[x]</math> a new multiplication, subject to the identity

: <math>x r = \sigma(r)x + \delta(r)</math>.

If ''δ'' = 0 (i.e., is the zero map) then the Ore extension is denoted ''R''[''x'';&thinsp;''σ'']. If ''σ'' = 1 (i.e., the [[identity map]]) then the Ore extension is denoted ''R''[''x'',&thinsp;''δ''&thinsp;] and is called a '''differential polynomial ring'''.

== Examples ==

The [[Weyl algebra]]s are Ore extensions, with ''R'' any commutative [[polynomial ring]], ''σ'' the identity ring [[endomorphism]], and ''δ'' the [[formal derivative|polynomial derivative]].  [[Ore algebra]]s are a class of iterated Ore extensions under suitable constraints that permit to develop a noncommutative extension of the theory of [[Gröbner bases]].

== Properties ==

* An Ore extension of a [[domain (ring theory)|domain]] is a domain.
* An Ore extension of a [[skew field]] is a non-commutative [[principal ideal domain]].
* If ''σ'' is an [[automorphism]] and ''R'' is a left [[Noetherian ring]] then the Ore extension ''R''[''λ'';&thinsp;''σ'',&thinsp;''δ''&thinsp;] is also left Noetherian.

== Elements ==

An element ''f'' of an Ore ring ''R'' is called
* '''twosided'''<ref>{{cite book|last=Jacobson|first=Nathan|author-link=Nathan Jacobson|title=Finite-Dimensional Division Algebras over Fields|date=1996|publisher=Springer}}</ref>  (or '''invariant'''<ref>{{cite book|last=Cohn|first=Paul M.|author-link=Paul Cohn|title=Skew Fields: Theory of General Division Rings|url=https://archive.org/details/skewfieldstheory0000cohn|url-access=registration|date=1995|publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]]}}</ref> ), if ''R·f = f·R'', and
* '''central''', if ''g·f = f·g'' for all ''g'' in ''R''.
